title: The Lisbon Regicide
summary: On 1 February 1908 King Carlos I and his heir Luís Filipe were shot dead in an open carriage crossing the Terreiro do Paço in Lisbon. The gunmen came from the republican fringe and were sheltered and armed by members of the Carbonária, and what they meant to end was the government of João Franco, who had dissolved parliament the previous May and was ruling by decree with the king’s consent. Franco’s government did not survive the killing. Carlos’s younger son came to the throne as Manuel II, eighteen years old and without preparation, and the ministries that followed tried to return the country to constitutional forms. The monarchy lasted another thirty-two months and never recovered the authority it lost in the square. It is in the atlas as the point at which the crisis of the constitutional monarchy stopped being parliamentary.
